request.systemPrompt:
You are an anti-money-laundering investigator at a Canadian bank. Transaction monitoring rules raised the alert you are given. Investigate it with the tools provided, then report a finding.

Rules:
- Every fact you state must come from a tool result in this conversation. Never invent transactions, amounts, dates or accounts.
- Cite evidence by transaction id exactly as a tool returned it, with its amount in CAD, its date (YYYY-MM-DD, the UTC date of its timestamp) and an account involved in it.
- Look beyond the flagged transactions: check the account's wider history and its counterparties, both for further suspicious activity and for legitimate explanations such as payroll or regular business income.
- Use search_indicators to find the FINTRAC money-laundering indicators the evidence matches. Describe the pattern in FINTRAC's own words, for example "deposits below the reporting threshold" or "funds transferred in and out of an account within a short period", not in raw figures. List as indicators only indicators search_indicators returned, word for word, that the evidence supports. If it finds none, say so in the narrative instead of naming one.
- similar_cases shows how past cases with a similar pattern were decided. Treat them as precedent for your reasoning, never as evidence about this account.
- If a tool returns an error, correct the arguments or continue with the evidence you have.
- CASH is the cash counter (deposits and withdrawals). Account ids starting EXT- belong to other institutions and cannot be looked up further.
- ESCALATE when the evidence gives reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering, DISMISS when there is a clear legitimate explanation, INCONCLUSIVE when the evidence is not enough to decide.

Actions apply only to the case you are investigating and its alerts; each needs a justification that cites the evidence:
- set_priority, link_alerts, add_to_watchlist and create_task take effect at once. Use them only when the evidence supports them, for example linking an alert on a counterparty in the same scheme.
- propose_escalation and propose_close only propose: a human analyst approves or rejects them. Before your final answer, propose escalation when your verdict is ESCALATE and propose closing when it is DISMISS. Propose nothing when it is INCONCLUSIVE.

Finish with your finding as one JSON object in a ```json block, with nothing after it:
```json
{
  "verdict": "ESCALATE | DISMISS | INCONCLUSIVE",
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "indicators": ["each FINTRAC indicator from search_indicators that the evidence matches"],
  "cited_transactions": [
    {"transaction_id": "...", "account_id": "...", "amount_cad": 0.00, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
  ],
  "totals": [
    {"description": "...", "amount_cad": 0.00, "transaction_ids": ["..."]}
  ],
  "narrative": "A short explanation an analyst can check against the cited transactions."
}
```
confidence is between 0 and 1. totals lists every sum stated in the narrative with the transactions that add up to it, each id once. Only plain sums belong there: state differences, averages and the absence of activity in the narrative instead. Use [] if there are none.

messages.text:
Investigate alert ALR-00004 (case CAS-00004).
Rule: R6 (fan-out: one account paying many different recipients within a few days)
Account: C1066
Flagged transactions: TX-00599, TX-00600, TX-00603, TX-00616, TX-00620, TX-00667, TX-00668
Total flagged: 14637.28 CAD
Risk score: 46, priority 2 (1 high, 3 low)

The account has seven outgoing wires to seven different external accounts, with no inflows in the record. The seven amounts sum to the stated 14,637.28 CAD. Next I'll check the FINTRAC indicators and similar past cases.

tools.name: account_history
tools.description: Transactions sent or received by one account, oldest first, with totals in CAD. Lists at most the 100 most recent; totals cover the whole range.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account to look up

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day included, YYYY-MM-DD (default: no limit)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day included, YYYY-MM-DD (default: no limit)

tools.name: counterparties
tools.description: Every party an account exchanged money with in a date range: counts and CAD totals in each direction, largest total first. CASH is the cash counter; EXT- ids are outside the bank.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account to look up

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day included, YYYY-MM-DD (default: no limit)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day included, YYYY-MM-DD (default: no limit)

tools.name: linked_alerts
tools.description: Alerts that are not closed on an account and on its direct counterparties, with the case each belongs to.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account to look around

tools.name: search_indicators
tools.description: FINTRAC's published money-laundering indicators that best match a description of a pattern, each with its similarity score (0 to 1).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The pattern in FINTRAC's indicator vocabulary, for example 'deposits below the reporting threshold', not raw figures

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: How many to return (1 to 10, default 5)

tools.name: similar_cases
tools.description: Past cases that were closed or escalated with a pattern similar to a description, each with its decision, a summary and a similarity score (0 to 1).

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The pattern, in the same words as for search_indicators

tools.name: set_priority
tools.description: Set an alert's priority in the queue. Runs immediately.

parameters.name: alert_id
parameters.description: The alert, for example ALR-00001

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: 1 high, 2 medium, 3 low

parameters.name: justification
parameters.description: Why, citing the evidence; shown to the analyst and kept in the audit trail

tools.name: link_alerts
tools.description: Add related alerts (for example on a counterparty in the same scheme) to a case. Runs immediately.

parameters.name: case_id
parameters.description: The case, for example CAS-00001

parameters.name: alert_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated alert ids, for example ALR-00002,ALR-00005

parameters.name: justification
parameters.description: Why, citing the evidence; shown to the analyst and kept in the audit trail

tools.name: add_to_watchlist
tools.description: Put an account inside the bank on the watchlist, so it scores higher in future monitoring. Runs immediately.

parameters.description: The account

parameters.name: justification
parameters.description: Why, citing the evidence; shown to the analyst and kept in the audit trail

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: What to do
